**Not accepted — CI is red, and it is a real regression from this PR.** PM round 19, session `session_01RV6yuVCxymHYE16PL9vQkE`. Sent back to the implementing dev; ⛔ no code touched from this seat.

```
FAIL examples/console-starter/test/vite-alias-closure.test.ts
     > console-starter vite alias table > reaches the workspace graph it is meant to cover
AssertionError: expected 401 to be greater than 500
  ❯ examples/console-starter/test/vite-alias-closure.test.ts:154:33
```

`Test (shard 3/4)`, head `4cd8c01f1`: **1 failed / 5524 passed**. ⛔ Not flaky and ⛔ not a re-run candidate — the test body ran and 430 other files in the same shard passed.

## The failing assertion is the one designed for exactly this

Its own preceding comment: *"Same guard for the walker: a resolution regression that walked … would make the closure assertion trivially true."* The floor exists to catch a walker that quietly stopped resolving, and `filesWalked` collapsing from >500 to **401** is that. It did its job.

## Diagnosis, offered to the dev to verify rather than adopt

This appears to be **the same defect class this PR already found and fixed once**: `scripts/check-i18n-call-site-keys.mjs`'s `resolveImport()` did not know `./i18n.js` addresses `i18n.ts`. Here a second consumer walks the workspace graph through the console-starter alias table, meets the now-explicit `./x.js` specifiers, cannot resolve them to `x.tsx`, and truncates the walk.

⚠️ Line 155 (`expect(closure.unresolvable).toEqual([])`) **never executed** — the throw came first — so whether that is also non-empty is unknown and may be the more direct symptom.

## The interesting part is why the sweep missed it

The PR enumerated its consumption radius mechanically and well: 625 rewritten specifiers searched, plain and regex-escaped, across all 66 files repo-wide that **address `packages/app-shell/src` by path**. That method is sound and it found two real pins.

But this consumer **names no app-shell path**. It reaches app-shell transitively, through the alias table, via its own resolver. So the blind spot has a shape: *a resolver that walks the graph, versus a file that mentions it.* I have asked for that class to be enumerated before the fix lands, because one such consumer existing means the class is real.

That is a correction to the method, not a criticism of it — mechanical radius enumeration is still far better than waiting for red, and it is what caught the two `check-i18n-call-site-keys` and `packages/i18n` regressions before CI ever saw them.

## Constraints given

⛔ **Do not lower the 500 floor and do not relax the assertion** — weakening a gate to get green is out of bounds. If the true post-fix count is legitimately different, report the measurement and route it rather than adjusting it.

Everything else in my review stands: surface verified against the declared set plus three declared breaches, `tsconfig.json` byte-identical, `SPECIFIER_DEBT` genuinely `new Map()`, and the `LOAD_DEBT` move accepted as the right bookkeeping. This is a fourth forced out-of-surface file, to be declared with the others.
